newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea May CPI rises 3.8 pct vs 5.1 pct yr ago.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea May CPI rises 3.8 pct vs 5.1 pct yr ago.

text.p: South Korea's consumer price index (CPI) rose 3.8 percent in May on the year, down from a 5.1 percent rise a year earlier, Ministry of Finance and Economy figures showed on Friday.
(base=1995 for May and April '97, and 1990 for May '96)
The May rise was the lowest monthly increase in 10 years, a ministry official said. In May 1987 the CPI rose 2.6 percent, he said.

A ministry official said the CPI in May slowed as prices for farm goods continued to stabilise due to favorable weather. Prices for agricultural, livestock and fisheries products rose a year-on-year 1.2 percent in the month.
Beef prices, excluding imports, fell 14.4 percent, and potatos dropped 34.9 percent, the ministry said.
Prices for industrial products rose a year-on-year 4.0 percent, led by a 25.5 percent rise in oil products.
But industrial product prices, excluding oil products, rose year-on-year 1.1 percent, the ministry said.
"The slowing economy and intensifying competition in distribution helped keep industrial prices in check," said Yoon Sung-ho, director of the ministry's price division.
Food prices rose year-on-year 2.2 percent in May, with prices for vegetables falling 9.5 percent year-on-year.
Prices for non-food products increased 4.5 percent.
The ministry said public utility fares increased 4.3 percent in May, and prices for services, such as private-sector education fees, rose 5.3 percent.
The CPI, South Korea's leading inflation indicator, rose 4.5 percent in all of 1996, down from a 4.7 percent rise in 1995, the ministry said.
It said the CPI rise would be around 4.5 percent this year.
